analysis_scope: offline static inventory of the original Graal Online Classic 1.8 APK

findings.impact: The native connector and game socket can communicate with remote endpoints.
findings.limit: This is expected for an online game and does not identify a vulnerable endpoint by itself.
findings.title: The application has network access

evidence: An exported component accepts graalclassic:// or graalclassicplus:// intent data.
findings.impact: Any installed application can request the activity, so URI action, data, and extras are an input boundary.
findings.limit: This audit did not send a malicious intent or claim code execution from the URI alone.
findings.title: An exported activity accepts custom Graal URI schemes

findings.confidence: confirmed capability, path boundaries reviewed locally
evidence: DEX strings include WebView, setJavaScriptEnabled, and addJavascriptInterface. Local smali review places the game WebView in QPlayActivity and the bridge call in the bundled Bolts app-link resolver.
findings.impact: QPlayActivity can load native-supplied URLs with JavaScript enabled. The separate Bolts resolver exposes a narrow JSON metadata bridge, so both paths deserve input and navigation review.
findings.limit: Static review does not prove that a remote page can reach the game WebView, the Bolts resolver, or every bridge method in a production run.
findings.title: The Java layer contains separate JavaScript-enabled WebView surfaces

findings.confidence: confirmed legacy string anchor, safe branch verified by local smali
evidence: The DEX string table contains onReceivedSslError and DISABLE_SSL_CHECK_FOR_TESTING. Local smali review resolves them to Facebook WebDialog, where the flag is false and the SSL-error handler calls SslErrorHandler.cancel() before dismissing the dialog.
findings.impact: This is a useful maintenance and call-graph anchor, but the reviewed Java path rejects WebView certificate errors rather than accepting them.
findings.limit: This finding does not describe the native CyaSSL connector and does not prove how unrelated WebViews handle errors. The fz_server_domain_ssl string is also only a configuration anchor here.
findings.title: Facebook WebDialog carries a disabled SSL-test flag

findings.confidence: confirmed legacy vocabulary, active suite selection unproven
evidence: libqplay.so contains RC4 and NULL cipher identifiers and TLS version strings.
findings.impact: If enabled by negotiation or configuration, legacy suites increase downgrade and confidentiality risk.
findings.limit: String presence does not show that a weak suite was negotiated. Separate IDA review found peer and hostname verification in the connector path.
findings.title: The bundled native TLS implementation contains legacy cipher names

findings.confidence: confirmed embedded legacy material, active trust use unproven
evidence: res/raw/fabzat_com.crt is a PEM certificate for admin.fabzat.com.
Its recorded validity ends at 2014-08-23T05:22:41 and its signature hash is sha1.
findings.impact: Any code that treats this file as a trust anchor or pinned service certificate cannot validate a current service chain after expiry.
findings.limit: The file's presence does not prove that startup or login consumes it. No live request was made.
findings.title: The APK carries an expired Fabzat certificate

findings.confidence: confirmed embedded bundle, active validation path separately reviewed
evidence: The ARM64 library contains 12820 bytes of trust text at file offset 3002104 with SHA-256 c87ea7bc32005cca699fb724ab455926fd852a1bd40ce0985aadf31a994878a0.
findings.impact: A connector that still validates only against this bundle can fail after a service certificate renewal.
findings.limit: The report does not claim that every native connection uses the bundle or that replacing it is safe without an authorized current chain.
findings.title: The native library embeds a fixed connector trust bundle

evidence: The extracted v1 certificate reports signature hash sha1 and fingerprint c63130fa95a05ec36c4f1dca30cf148a0b2fb3818c794899cd426206f5067c02.
findings.impact: SHA-1 is legacy signing metadata and can complicate installation or trust decisions on modern tooling.
findings.limit: This does not mean the APK was forged. The report does not independently verify every APK signature scheme.
findings.title: The APK v1 signing certificate uses SHA-1

evidence: readelf reports non-executable GNU_STACK program headers for the packaged shared libraries.
findings.impact: This is a useful mitigation against one class of memory corruption exploit.
findings.limit: It does not establish full RELRO, complete control-flow integrity, or safe input handling.
findings.title: Packaged native libraries do not request an executable stack

reproduction.side_effects: Reads the APK and writes only the requested JSON report. Temporary ELF and certificate files are removed on exit.
